A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Persuaficial research. Their main text, equations, six figures, 32 tables, and Appendices A–J are available for comparison; pagination and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-quality evaluations, multilingual persuasion-detection experiments, linguistic feature analyses, and an auxiliary authorship-classification study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised linguistic effect sizes and feature rankings.

M1.justification: The four generation approaches, prompting procedures, generation and detection models, zero-shot classification, and StyloMetrix feature extraction are unchanged. The substantive revision concerns the statistical analysis of their outputs.

E1.justification: Both versions use SemEval 2023 Task 3, DIPROMATS 2024, and ChangeMyView, covering the same six languages and four generation scenarios. The linguistic analysis remains English-only. Added discussion of parliamentary-debate data does not introduce its experimental use.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain GPT-4.1 Mini, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Gemma 3 27B, and Llama 3.3 70B, together with the human-written reference conditions. Appendix H/Table 16 retains RF, XGB, and LGBM. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The linguistic comparison metric changes from pooled-standard-deviation Cohen’s d in v1 Appendix I to paired-difference standardization in v2 Section 5.2. Dataset sampling, generation and classification temperatures, F1 evaluation, and the auxiliary classification split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The auxiliary StyloMetrix classification analysis in Appendix H, its experimental design, and Table 16 results are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or case study is introduced; the central linguistic study receives statistical and result revisions.

E5.justification: The effect-size estimator underlying the entire linguistic feature-ranking analysis is replaced: v1 divides the group mean difference by pooled standard deviation, whereas v2 divides the mean paired difference by its standard deviation. This substantially revises statistical estimation for RQ2. Paired Wilcoxon tests and Benjamini–Hochberg correction were already present in v1 and are retained.

E6.justification: Table 5 and Tables 17–32 replace effect sizes, feature membership, and rankings. For GPT-4.1 Mini paraphrasing, lemma type-token ratio moves from fourth at 0.3713 to first at 0.9218 under the changed normalization (Table 17). Section 5.3 also narrows the punctuation finding to lower period density in Llama texts. Detection and auxiliary classification scores in Tables 3–4 and 8–16 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The pooled-variance definition in v1 Appendix I is replaced by explicit paired-difference definitions in v2 Section 5.2, Equations 1–4. This changes the mathematical quantity being reported, rather than merely its notation or location. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same benchmark, detection-difficulty findings, and novelty claims about comparing human and AI-generated persuasive language. The conclusion’s scientific claims remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly states that the analysis characterizes differences within persuasive texts without isolating persuasion-specific features from broader AI–human writing differences. This adds a substantive interpretive boundary. Existing English-only and zero-shot limitations and most mechanism explanations are retained.

D1.justification: Footnote 2 replaces the anonymous 4open.science repository reference with a named GitHub repository for code, data, and prompts, changing the reported access information. Existing API identifiers, temperatures, prompt templates, annotation instructions, and data-splitting details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Labruna et al. (2026) and discussion of MIPD by Modzelewski et al. (2024a), and expands discussion of the previously cited SlavicNLP taxonomy. These are limited contextual additions; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The statistical explanation is rewritten and brought into Section 5.2, while Appendix I is refocused on significance testing. Other edits include localized clarifications, affiliation reordering, acknowledgments, and unnumbered Limitations and Ethics headings. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: All six figures and 32 tables remain. Figure 1 receives a revised caption and placement, Table 5 changes its effect-size column notation, and appendix feature labels and float placement are adjusted. The established visual organization is retained; numerical revisions are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies its revised paired-effect calculation and adds a useful boundary against interpreting general AI–human differences as persuasion-specific. However, Tables 26 and 30 newly report identical values and rankings for all 20 features for Gemma and Gemini subtle rewriting, whereas v1 reported distinct results. This unexplained duplication leaves part of the revised evidence’s reliability unresolved, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
